skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through the inference.sh belt CLI, with configurable dimensions, frame rate, duration, props, and codec options.
skill.summary: Generate MP4 videos from Remotion component code using inference.sh.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby or shell backtick alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, table field names, and TSX template literals. The actionable risks are the skill dependency on external CLI commands and the required use of inference.sh, which sends code and props to a remote service. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the exact belt app run infsh/remotion-render workflow, or require explicit user approval for other belt commands.

remediation.issue: Remote rendering of user-provided code and props
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that TSX code and props are sent to inference.sh, and advise them not to include secrets or private assets.
Pin installation guidance to a reviewed release and host marketplace images from a controlled or bundled asset path.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |

| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |

"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export

content.value_statement: Creating video from React animation code often requires a full Remotion setup. This skill sends TSX components to inference.sh and returns rendered MP4 videos.
actual_capabilities: Renders default-exported Remotion React components into MP4 output through the belt CLI.
Supports width, height, FPS, duration, codec, composition ID, and props inputs.
Documents common Remotion APIs such as AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, and interpolate.
Shows examples for fade-ins, counters, spring motion, props, and sequence-based scenes.
Provides Python SDK examples for batch rendering and streaming progress.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, the belt CLI, and network access.
Sends component code and props to a remote rendering service.
Does not provide local rendering, asset validation, or secret filtering.
Only documents React and Remotion imports; other runtime APIs may fail.

use_cases.title: Create Social Motion Clips
use_cases.description: Render short branded animations from React components for launch posts, product updates, and internal announcements.

use_cases.title: Generate Data-Driven Videos
use_cases.description: Use props to render repeatable video variants for metrics, rankings, or customer-specific reports.

use_cases.title: Prototype Remotion Scenes
use_cases.description: Test Remotion ideas quickly without preparing a local render project or build pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Intro
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a three-second MP4 with a centered title, 1920x1080, 30 FPS, and a dark background.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Counter Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a five-second square video with an animated percentage counter, smooth opacity changes, and clear typography.

prompt_templates.title: Use Props for Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion video that accepts title, subtitle, and accent color props, then render one branded MP4 variant.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sequenced Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a 12-second explainer with three timed sequences, spring transitions, image placeholders, and 1080p output settings.

output_examples.input: A user requests a five-second animated launch title with a dark background and 30 FPS output.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a rendered MP4 link, the chosen render settings, and a short description of the animation.

output_examples.input: A product team needs three video variants with different titles, subtitles, and accent colors.
output_examples.output: The assistant renders separate MP4 files and lists which props were used for each variant.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for progress updates during a longer Remotion render.
output_examples.output: The assistant streams render progress when supported and reports the final video URL when processing completes.

best_practices: Keep TSX components focused, deterministic, and small before sending them to the renderer.
Review code and props for secrets, private URLs, and customer data before rendering.
Specify duration, FPS, width, and height explicitly for predictable output.
anti_patterns: Do not send API keys, private tokens, or confidential data inside props or component code.
Do not assume unsupported imports or browser APIs will work in the remote renderer.
Do not run installation commands without reviewing the source and confirming user intent.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React components written for Remotion into MP4 videos through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require local Remotion setup?
faq.answer: No. The examples use the belt CLI and a remote inference.sh renderer instead of a local Remotion project.

faq.question: Can I pass custom text or colors?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented props field can pass values such as titles, subtitles, and styling options.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is my code rendered locally?
faq.answer: No. The skill sends component code and props to inference.sh for remote rendering.

faq.question: What should I avoid sending?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, private files, customer data, and asset URLs that should not leave your environment.
